name: Algomo
summary: AI inbound agent and website personalization for B2B — qualifies visitors by identity, holds contextual conversations and books meetings from your existing traffic.
best_for: teams that want one AI agent on their own website for support and inbound sales, priced by the work it does rather than by seat, and who want to start self-serve on a free plan
skip_if: you need SOC 2 evidence, more than five users or a second agent without an enterprise contract, or you cannot accept the agent going quiet when its monthly credits run out
honest_knock: The credit model is clear on paper with one opaque step: whether a conversation was 'useful', and so billed at five credits, is decided by a language model after it closes. Algomo shows the verdict and lets you contest it, but the bill rests on a classifier you do not control. The other edges are deliberate. You cannot buy top-ups, so a traffic spike ends with the agent switched off rather than with an overage invoice; nothing is prorated when you change rungs; and cancelling drops the account to Free, where any balance above 140 credits is trimmed. On security, Algomo states that it has not completed a SOC 2 audit, and conversations go to OpenAI by default, with Anthropic, Google and Mistral models reached through OpenRouter only if you select one.

pricing.entry_price_terms: a month for 2,000 credits up to $4,300 for 200,000
pricing.notes: (re-read 2026-10-22 on algomo.com/pricing and its markdown version, algomo.com/pricing.md) Algomo now publishes a complete self-serve price list, and it replaces the single '$200 a month' starting price we had recorded since July. There are three plans. Free is $0 with 100 credits a month, one user, one workspace and one agent, and needs no credit card. Business is a ladder of fixed rungs rather than a slider: 2,000 credits for $50 a month, 4,000 for $100, 8,000 for $200, 16,000 for $400, 25,000 for $600, 40,000 for $950, 60,000 for $1,400, 80,000 for $1,850, 100,000 for $2,250, 150,000 for $3,300 and 200,000 for $4,300, each with up to five users on one workspace and one agent. A budget between two rungs buys the lower one. Paid yearly, every rung costs ten months: $500 a year at the bottom and $43,000 at the top, which the table shows as a 17% to 28% saving against the $50-per-2,000 base rate once the volume discount (4% at 25,000 credits, rising to 14% at 200,000) is added. Enterprise is 'Contact us' and adds unlimited users and agents, several workspaces, SSO, SLAs, a DPA, a security review and, only when a buyer's procurement asks for it, a contract that runs for a year. The unit behind every rung is the same on Free and Business: five credits for a conversation the agent helped with, five more for every further ten replies, nothing for a conversation that went nowhere, and a hundredth of a credit for each workflow step that calls an outside service or each knowledge-base lookup that finds something. Algomo's own estimate is that $50 covers about 400 useful conversations a month.
